keyVerseText: And GOD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually. every: or, the whole imagination: the Hebrew word signifieth not only the imagination, but also the purposes and desires continually: Heb. every day
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun מַחֲשָׁבָה (machăshâbâh) derives from the root חָשַׁב (châshab), which fundamentally means to weave or interpenetrate, extending metaphorically to mean to devise, consider, or imagine. This root conveys not merely abstract thought but the deliberate crafting or fabricating of ideas, plans, or devices. Thus, the root sense enriches the English gloss of 'thought' or 'device' by emphasizing the intentional and constructed nature of mental activity, as if thoughts are woven or engineered with purpose.
usageInScripture: Throughout its 56 occurrences, מַחֲשָׁבָה is translated variously as 'thoughts,' 'devices,' 'purposes,' and 'imagination,' indicating a semantic range that includes both intellectual reflection and practical planning. The frequent rendering as 'the thoughts' or 'devices' highlights its dual abstract and concrete senses—referring either to internal mental processes or to deliberate plans and contrivances. This diversity reveals the word's flexibility in Scripture to describe everything from human intentions to divine counsel, underscoring the depth and complexity of what is encompassed by 'thought' in the biblical worldview.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מַחֲשָׁבָה as the weaving or fabricating of thoughts and plans invites believers to recognize the profound nature of human and divine cognition. It reminds us that our inner imaginations and purposes are not random but are constructed with intention, reflecting the image of a purposeful Creator. The word also challenges Christians to consider the alignment of their own devised plans with God's perfect and higher thoughts, as human thoughts can be both good and evil. This insight calls for humility and dependence on God's wisdom, acknowledging that His purposes transcend human understanding and that our hearts’ imaginations must be submitted to His sovereign will.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 6:5 states, 'And GOD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.' Here, מַחֲשָׁבָה conveys not just fleeting ideas but the continuous, deliberate fabric of human intentions and desires. This word deepens the verse's meaning by emphasizing that mankind’s inner mental constructs were persistently evil, illustrating the pervasive corruption of human nature prior to the Flood. It serves as a sobering reminder of the seriousness with which God views the inner workings of the heart and mind.
